coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: William J. Rutter Community Center
record.summary: A ~150,000 sq ft community center at 1675 Owens St housing the Bakar Fitness & Recreation Center, the Mission Bay Conference Center, administrative offices and a restaurant/food court, opened 2005 as part of Mission Bay's first development phase in Legorreta's contemporary Mexican-modernist style.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate; the west edge is idealized to a straight line (2 points instead of the OSM trace's 3, dropping a sub-meter digitizing jog), not a surveyed change. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson and DataSF's Assessor tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 at 675 Nelson Rising Lane alone is ~13 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for this record.
notes.digitized_from: OpenStreetMap (way 84812339, name=William J. Rutter Center, 1675 Owens St). Its own small mid-edge digitizing jog on the west wall was straightened into a clean 4-corner quadrilateral 2026-09-22 (see digitization_method).

record.notes: ~150,000-156,600 sq ft (sources vary), four to five stories; houses the Bakar Fitness & Recreation Center, Mission Bay Conference Center, administrative offices and a restaurant/food court. Architect Legorreta Arquitectos (Ricardo and Victor Legorreta) with MBT Architecture as associate/executive architect, in Legorreta's contemporary Mexican-modernist style. Opened 2005 as part of Mission Bay's first development phase (year only; exact month not confirmed by a primary source). Per UCSF's own Dec 2024-updated campus map, this is Block 21B; the adjoining Community Center Garage to its west is the separate Block 21A (data/manual/ucsf_community_center_garage.geojson).
